sum: A seven-day trek from Lukla to Namche Bazaar, Tengboche monastery and Khumjung, with views of Everest, Lhotse and Ama Dablam and a highest point of 3,880 m.

guide.note: Khumbu has not enforced the national guide requirement, and this is the busiest and best-marked trail in the country, so finding the way is not the issue. A licensed guide is still useful on a short first trek: they set a pace that suits the Namche hill, hold beds in peak season and deal with the airline when flights are delayed.

access: Fly to Lukla and back. Flights leave soon after dawn from Kathmandu or, in the spring and autumn peaks, from Manthali in Ramechhap, and are cancelled when cloud covers the Lukla approach. On a one-week trip a lost day matters, so keep a spare one in hand.

photo.a: Trekkers follow a path across a grassy ridge dotted with pines, with the snow wall of Everest and Lhotse on the left and the sharp white peak of Ama Dablam on the right under a clear blue sky.
photo.c: Everest, Lhotse and Ama Dablam from the ridge above Namche Bazaar

includes: porter in most packages (the cheapest tiers leave one out)
Sagarmatha park and Khumbu municipality permits
lodge beds and three meals a day on the trek
airport transfers; Kathmandu hotel nights in some packages

permits.name: Sagarmatha National Park entry permit
permits.where: At the park gate in Monjo, or in advance at the park counter in the Tourist Service Centre, Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu.

permits.name: Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality entry permit
permits.where: At the municipality's tourist information centre in Lukla when you land, or at the Monjo checkpoint if you walk in from the road. It cannot be bought in Kathmandu.

transportText: Flights to Lukla and back, from Kathmandu or (in the busy months) from Manthali with a night drive to the airstrip
tips: Even in spring, pack a down jacket and a warm sleeping bag. Tengboche nights are at or below freezing for most of the trekking year.
Namche has cash machines, but they are often empty or offline. Bring enough rupees from Kathmandu for the whole week.
Walk the Namche hill slowly enough to hold a conversation. Arriving an hour later costs nothing; arriving exhausted costs you the next day.
With children or older walkers, add a night at Monjo on the way up to split the climb to Namche.
Treat all drinking water. Lodges along the whole route sell boiled or filtered water for refills.

days.t: Fly to Lukla, walk to Phakding
days.note: A morning flight and an easy three hours down the valley past mani walls and small farms. Phakding is lower than Lukla, which makes the first night easier on your body.

The trail stays near the river as far as Monjo, where permits are checked, then crosses the high bridge and climbs 600 m through pine forest to Namche. This is the hardest day of the trek. Go slowly, drink often and expect to feel the height when you arrive.
med: Um Hong Gil Namche Community Hospital

days.note: Climb past the national park visitor centre to the Syangboche shelf and along to the hotel terrace, about 440 m above town. Everest, Lhotse and Ama Dablam are in front of you by mid-morning. Have tea, walk back down and rest.
med: Um Hong Gil Namche Community Hospital

days.note: The trail contours high above the Dudh Koshi with the mountains ahead all morning, drops through pine forest to the river at Phunki Tenga, then climbs 600 m in long zigzags to the monastery. Try to arrive in time for the afternoon prayers.

days.t: Tengboche to Namche by way of Khumjung
days.note: Go back down to the river and up to the junction at Sanasa, then take the upper path to Khumjung to see the school and the monastery. Cross the shelf past the Syangboche airstrip and drop into Namche. If you are tired, the direct trail saves an hour.
med: Um Hong Gil Namche Community Hospital

days.note: The whole valley in one long, mostly downhill day, with a last hour uphill into Lukla. If your knees complain or your flight is a day later, break it with a night in Monjo or Phakding.
Morning flight to Kathmandu or Manthali, weather permitting. A cancelled flight means another night in Lukla, so do not plan to leave Nepal the same evening.
